traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia, Oemleria cerasiformis (read 2026-10-17): each of the five free pistils can ripen into a plum-like drupe, reddish pink turning deep blue. Stated here so the genus does not take Rosaceae's aggregate fruit.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full, as Osmaronia: dioecious; stamens 15 in 3 rows, 10 with the petals and 5 lower on the disk; pistils 5, distinct, in the superior-ovaried tribe Drupeae; in the pistillate flower the stamens are abortive. The Flora of North America's genus (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read): stamens 15 in 3 series; carpels usually 5. Drawn as a staminate flower with its pistils.
